updates.summary: Recommendations of Jamaica's National AI Task Force, presented to the Office of the Prime Minister as the basis for a National AI Policy. After a Cabinet decision, the Minister responsible for science and technology in the Office of the Prime Minister convened a reconstituted 23-member Task Force on 19 Feb 2026 and charged it with a draft national AI policy within six to nine months and a draft legislative framework within twelve months, building on these recommendations and the UNESCO AI Readiness Assessment. updates.issuing_body: Chamber of Deputies of Paraguay; bill by Deputies Rodrigo Gamarra, Rocío Abed, Miguel Del Puerto, Del Pilar Vázquez and Hugo Meza
updates.summary: Chamber of Deputies bill declaring the development and implementation of AI of national interest as a strategic tool for modernising the country's sectors. In 20 articles it would make the ICT ministry (MITIC) the enforcement authority, in charge of national AI policies, supervision and a National Register of AI Systems; set principles for ethical AI use stressing privacy, prevention of bias and discrimination, and algorithmic transparency; prohibit AI for indiscriminate surveillance; require ethical audits of systems affecting fundamental rights; set sanctions for misuse; and create a National Committee on AI Ethics and Regulation, with tax incentives, research and education measures.
updates.notes: Presented in the Chamber of Deputies shortly before 1 May 2025 by five deputies; a press report of 1 May 2025 also names Deputies Carlos Núñez Salinas and Johanna Ortega among its sponsors. The Chamber's bulletin item of 2 May 2025 gives the title as 'Que promueve el uso de la Inteligencia Artificial (IA) en favor del desarrollo económico, social, científico y cultural del país'; later references give the shorter title. The Committee on Social Equity and Equal Rights of Men and Women, chaired by Deputy Abed, convened a public hearing on the bill for 4 Jun 2025. On 27 Oct 2025 the Committee on National Defence, Security, Intelligence and Internal Order continued studying it; it still awaited technical opinions from MITIC, which would be the main regulator, and from the Ministry of the Interior. A separate Senate bill regulating AI systems, presented in May 2025, is PY-01.

updates.summary: Policy of Paraguay's Supreme Court of Justice guiding magistrates and judicial staff on the ethical, responsible and transparent use of AI systems, including in-house, acquired and licensed systems. Under a principle of human oversight it lists permitted supporting uses and forbids delegating decisions to AI, fully automating processes that affect fundamental rights, using AI to determine guilt or innocence, and setting penalties without human intervention. Parties must be told when AI is used, generative-AI text must be disclosed and prompts documented, and wholly opaque systems are banned. Further rules cover non-discrimination, data protection and security, and AI literacy training.
